name: Zygomatic arch reduction / reduction malarplasty

lead: Reduction malarplasty cuts and repositions the cheekbone (zygoma) or zygomatic arch to narrow a wide or prominent midface. The result is a slimmer, softer face shape, visible after healing. Surgeons describe it as one of the more commonly requested facial-contour procedures in East Asia.

Osteotomies are made in the malar complex or zygomatic arch and the bone is repositioned and fixed. Techniques have moved from coronal-incision approaches, which leave a scalp scar and carry facial-nerve risk, toward intraoral and limited-incision methods. The literature is mostly surgeon case series and technique papers. In looksmaxxing forums the related ZSO term mostly appears in discussions about the opposite aim, projecting cheekbones.

paras: It is planned with imaging and done under general anaesthetic through coronal, intraoral, preauricular or small percutaneous incisions. Swelling and bone healing take weeks to months before the final shape shows.
Reported concerns include scars and facial-nerve injury with some approaches, and zygomatic nonunion after surgery. It is major bone surgery performed by trained surgeons.

angle.text: Reduction malarplasty narrows wide or prominent cheekbones by cutting and repositioning the bone, giving a slimmer, softer face shape visible after healing. It is among the more commonly requested facial-contour procedures in East Asia, described mainly in surgeon case series.

lead: Reduction malarplasty is a facial-bone surgery that narrows a wide or prominent cheekbone (zygoma) by cutting and repositioning the malar complex or zygomatic arch.[1][2] Published authors describe it as one of the more commonly requested facial-contour procedures in East Asia and as rarely performed in the West.[1][3]

Techniques have evolved from coronal-incision approaches, which leave a scalp scar and carry facial-nerve risk, toward intraoral and limited-incision osteotomies.[4][3] The literature is made up of surgeon case series and technique descriptions; randomized trials were not found.

In looksmaxxing forums the term ZSO (zygomatic skeletal osteotomy) appears mostly in discussions about the opposite aim, projecting or repositioning cheekbones, and posters often compare it with malar implants and midface advancement.

paras: An early technique used a coronal incision and either transposition osteoplasty of the malar complex or its removal and refixation.[1] Later authors described intraoral approaches intended to avoid visible scars, facial-nerve injury and long operative times.[4][2] A retrospective study of 418 cases reported an L-shaped osteotomy through an intraoral approach intended to allow control of the degree of reduction.[3] A percutaneous approach using small 3-mm incisions has also been described.[5]

Zygomatic nonunion, in which the cut bone fails to heal, has been reported as a complication in the literature.[6] The authors of intraoral and limited-incision methods cite scars and facial-nerve injury as drawbacks of coronal approaches.[4]
Published human studies are retrospective surgical case series and technique reports, including a 418-case series from 2009.[3] No randomized controlled trials were found among the sources reviewed.

A looksmax.org thread shows a user asking whether a ZSO or malarplasty with autologous bone would help the eye area, and a reply attributing flat cheekbones to a recessed maxilla and suggesting a LeFort III osteotomy instead. This reflects a common forum framing in which cheek appearance is linked to midface projection.

lore.intro: On looksmax.org the ZSO is discussed within the broader topic of cheekbone and midface surgery.

claims.claim: Flat cheekbones are really a recessed maxilla problem rather than a cheek problem
